validity.recommendation: Treat as single-source (OPEC-only) and independently unverified. Remove the URUK/Jafar Dhia Jafar PDF from Capacity [ref] and Diameter [ref] (it does not mention this pipeline). Seek a primary Iraqi Oil Ministry / North Gas Company / SOMO source that actually names a Kirkuk-area North Gas Company dry-gas trunk to Taji before treating the 438 km / 16 in / 150 MMcf/d specs as corroborated; otherwise flag row as low-confidence OPEC-table artifact.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: The gem.wiki page's ONLY citation is 'Annual Statistical Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75' (wiki_citations.json shows a single OPEC ASB backlink). Web results confirm the GEM figures (438 km, 16 in, ~operating, Iraq Ministry of Oil) trace verbatim to that OPEC ASB 2012 pipeline table entry. That is a single origin. NO independent source I could find names a 'North Gas-Taji' gas pipeline or reproduces its specs. The currently-cited spec ref for BOTH Capacity and Diameter (iraqenergy.org Jafar-Dhia-Jafar-URUK.pdf) returns HTTP 200 but url_verifier finds neither 'Taji' nor 'North Gas' in it, and WebFetch confirms the PDF does not mention Taji, North Gas Company, 438 km, 16 in, or 150 MMcf/d at all -- so that ref does NOT support the values it is attached to (orphan/mis-attached ref). Independent Iraqi press about gas supply to Taji describes a DIFFERENT line: the Oil Pipelines Company's 2024 rehabilitation of a 12-inch dry-gas pipeline from the East Baghdad field to Taji power station (12 in, East Baghdad origin), not a 16-inch North Gas Company trunk. North Gas Company (public co., founded 1998, based at the northern Kirkuk-area gas fields) does produce dry gas piped to power and cement plants in northern and central Iraq (rawabetcenter history), so a legacy Kirkuk-area -> Baghdad/Taji dry-gas trunk is PLAUSIBLE as the physical referent -- but its name and specs remain unconfirmed by any independent source. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission line (dry gas), not one of the GulfPub crude/NGL Iraq lines; no oil-line collision. DUPLICATE: distinct from sister North Gas Company rows P2231 (North Gas-Baiji, 145 km/24 in) and P2232 (North Gas-K1, 34 km/18 in), and from Taji-side rows P1845 (Taji-South Baghdad) and P4054 (Taji-Duara); not an obvious relabel/segment double-count of any roster PID. SPEC red flags (secondary, all unresolved without the OPEC table itself): (a) 438 km is ~2x the ~218 km straight-line Kirkuk(North Gas hub ~35.47N,44.39E)->Taji(~33.51N,44.23E), implying either a looping corridor or an inflated figure; (b) capacity 150 MMcf/d is 30x-170x the sister North Gas lines' OPEC-derived capacities (P2231=0.89, P2232=5.26 MMcf/d), suggesting inconsistent unit handling across this OPEC-sourced batch. Bottom line: real-enough physical referent is plausible but the specific named/specced entity rests on ONE aggregate OPEC table row with zero independent corroboration and a mis-attached spec ref -> existence/spec concern, not a confirm.

routes.start_name: North Gas Company gas complex, Kirkuk area, Iraq (dry-gas hub of the northern fields)
routes.end_name: Taji power station, Al-Taji, north of Baghdad, Iraq
routes.corridor_desc: Best-defensible corridor: from the North Gas Company dry-gas complex serving the northern Kirkuk-area fields, running south/southeast down the Kirkuk-Tikrit-Samarra-Baghdad axis (Kirkuk -> Salah al-Din governorate -> northern Baghdad governorate) to the Taji power station cluster ~20 km north of Baghdad. Endpoints are reasonably fixed (Kirkuk North Gas hub start ~35.47N,44.39E; Taji power station end ~33.51N,44.23E, from GE/Wikipedia). The intermediate path is INFERRED, not sourced, so the bound is loose. Note the sheet's 438 km length is ~2x the ~218 km great-circle Kirkuk->Taji distance, so either the real line loops (e.g. via Baiji/K-stations to the west) or the length is overstated; no waypoint coordinates are asserted because none could be independently sourced.
routes.researcher_notes: End (Taji power station, Baghdad) is supported independently by GE's Taji plant press release and the Wikipedia Iraq power-stations list (both verify 'Taji'+'Baghdad'). Start (North Gas Company dry-gas hub, Kirkuk-area northern fields) is supported by rawabetcenter's North Gas Company history (dry gas to northern/central Iraq power/cement plants); Kirkuk city coordinates (~35.47N,44.39E) used as a defensible proxy for the company's northern-fields hub. No coordinate was invented: only named-place coordinates (Kirkuk, Taji-1) are used; intermediate waypoints left empty because no source pins them. Suggested accuracy low -- endpoints defensible, path inferred, and the length figure is internally inconsistent with the endpoint separation.

summary: P2233 North Gas-Taji: CONCERN (existence + secondary spec) -- specs (438 km/16 in/150 MMcf/d) rest solely on OPEC ASB 2012 p.75, no independent naming, and the cited URUK PDF does not mention the line at all; plausible legacy North Gas->Taji dry-gas trunk but unverified; proposed corridor Kirkuk North Gas hub->Taji power station at LOW accuracy.
